title: San Francisco algorithmic rent-setting ban
requirement: Landlords are prohibited from using algorithmic devices or revenue management software that use non-public competitor data to set, recommend, or advise on rents or occupancy levels. Additionally, it is unlawful to sell, license, or provide such devices to San Francisco landlords.
requirement_es: Se prohíbe a los propietarios utilizar dispositivos algorítmicos o programas de gestión de ingresos que utilicen datos no públicos de competidores para fijar, recomendar o asesorar sobre los alquileres o los niveles de ocupación. Además, es ilegal vender, licenciar o proporcionar dichos dispositivos a propietarios de San Francisco.

exemptions.description: Products used for the purpose of establishing rent or income limits in accordance with affordable housing program guidelines of a local, state, or federal government.

clauses.note: product used for establishing rent or income limits in accordance with affordable housing program guidelines

exemptions.description: Reports that publish existing rental data in an aggregated manner but do not recommend rents or occupancy levels for future leases.

penalty: Civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation, injunctive relief, restitution/return of illegal profits, and reasonable attorney's fees and costs. Each separate month a violation continues and each separate residential dwelling unit constitutes a separate violation.
quoted_span: It shall be unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device described in subdivision (a) when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in San Francisco. Each separate month that a violation exists or continues, and each separate residential dwelling unit for which the landlord used the algorithmic device, shall constitute a separate and distinct violation.

issues: The quote specifically supports the prohibition on landlords using algorithmic devices to set rents/occupancy levels and unit/month violation structure, but does not explicitly mention the sale/licensing prohibition, the $1,000 penalty amount, the affordable housing exemption, or the effective date.

title: Just Cause Eviction Protections
requirement: After a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied residential property for 30 days, a landlord cannot terminate the tenancy without stated at-fault or no-fault just cause.
requirement_es: Después de que un inquilino haya ocupado continua y legalmente una propiedad residencial durante 30 días, el arrendador no puede rescindir el contrato de alquiler sin una causa justificada culpable o no culpable debidamente indicada.

clauses.note: After a Tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a Residential Real Property for thirty (30) days

Dormitories owned and operated by higher education or K-12 school

After a Tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a Residential Real Property
for thirty (30) days, the Owner of the Residential Real Property shall not terminate
the Tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate
Tenancy. The provisions of this section related to the termination of Tenants shall
not apply to Mobilehomes or Mobilehome Spaces in Mobilehome Parks subject to the termination
provisions of the Mobilehome Residency Law, Civil Code section 798.56, as applicable.

title: No-Fault Eviction Relocation Assistance or Rent Waiver
requirement: If terminating a tenancy for no-fault just cause, the landlord must provide direct relocation assistance or waive rent for the final 3 months, equal to 3 months of the tenant's rent.
requirement_es: Si se rescinde un contrato de alquiler por una causa justificada no culpable, el propietario debe proporcionar asistencia directa de reubicación o condonar el alquiler durante los últimos 3 meses, por un monto equivalente a 3 meses del alquiler del inquilino.

clauses.note: Tenancy for which just cause is required

exemptions.description: Tenant found at fault by a government agency or court for conditions triggering an order or need to vacate
Properties exempt from just cause under section 8-3120(e)

precedence.source_language: The relocation assistance or Rent waiver required by this section shall be credited against any other relocation assistance required by any other law.

penalty: Failure to strictly comply renders the notice of termination void.
quoted_span:
The amount of relocation assistance or Rent waiver shall be equal to three (3) months
of the Tenant's Rent that was in effect when the Owner issued the notice to terminate
the Tenancy. Any relocation assistance shall be provided within fifteen (15) calendar
days of service of the notice.

title: Annual Allowable Rent Increase Cap
requirement: Landlords may not increase rent on residential real property or mobilehome spaces by more than 3% or 80% of the change in the Consumer Price Index (whichever is less) and may not impose more than one rent increase in any 12-month period. If the CPI change is negative, no rent increase is permitted.
requirement_es: Los arrendadores no pueden aumentar el alquiler de bienes raíces residenciales o espacios de casas móviles en más del 3% o el 80% del cambio en el Índice de Precios al Consumidor (lo que sea menor) y no pueden imponer más de un aumento en cualquier período de 12 meses. Si el IPC es negativo, no se permite ningún aumento.

quoted_span:
Increases in Rent on Residential Real Property or Mobilehome Spaces in the City of
Santa Ana in excess of three percent (3%), or eighty (80%) of the change in the Consumer
Price Index, whichever is less, and more than one Rent Increase in any twelve (12)
month period, are prohibited, unless expressly exempt under the Costa-Hawkins Rental
Housing Act codified in California Civil Code section 1954.50, et seq., or the Mobilehome Residency Law codified in California Civil Code sections 798, et seq. If the change in the Consumer Price Index is negative, no Rent
Increase is permitted. The term Consumer Price Index means, at the time of the adjustment
calculation completed by the City pursuant to subsection (b), the percentage increase
in the United State Consumer Price Index for all Urban Consumers in the Los Angeles-Long
Beach-Anaheim Metropolitan Area published by the Bureau of Labor Statistics, not seasonally
adjusted, for the most recent twelve (12) month period ending prior to the City's
calculation pursuant to subsection (b). A violation of this section occurs upon the
service of notice or demand for a prohibited increase in Rent.

requirement_es: Los arrendadores no pueden desalojar a un inquilino residencial excepto si demuestran una de las causas justificadas establecidas por la ley.

title: Jersey City Algorithmic Rent-Fixing Prohibition
requirement: Landlords and their agents are prohibited from subscribing to, contracting with, or exchanging value for the services of a pricing service provider that coordinates nonpublic competitor rental data, and service providers may not facilitate agreements not to compete.
requirement_es: Se prohíbe a los arrendadores y sus agentes suscribirse, contratar o intercambiar valor por los servicios de un proveedor que coordine datos no públicos de competidores, y los proveedores de servicios no pueden facilitar acuerdos contrarios a la competencia.

Inpatient medical care, licensed long-term care, and detention or correctional facilities

exchange anything of value in return for the services of a Service Provider.
b.No service provider shall facilitate an agreement not to compete among real estate lessors with respect to any
aspect of residential dwelling units, including rental pricing, fees, or any other rental terms.

title: San Francisco Annual Allowable Rent Increase
requirement: Landlords may only increase rent once per year by up to 60% of the regional CPI increase, capped at an absolute maximum of 7%. Unused increases may be banked and imposed on subsequent anniversary dates.
requirement_es: Los propietarios solo pueden aumentar el alquiler una vez al año hasta el 60% del aumento del IPC regional, con un tope máximo absoluto del 7%. Los aumentos no utilizados se pueden acumular y aplicar en fechas de aniversario posteriores.

title: Just cause eviction requirements and permitted grounds
requirement: A landlord may only recover possession of a rental unit for one of the specified just-cause grounds, which must be the dominant motive for eviction and stated in writing in the notice to vacate.
requirement_es: El arrendador solo puede recuperar la posesión de una unidad de alquiler por uno de los motivos de causa justa especificados, el cual debe ser el motivo dominante del desalojo y constar por escrito en el aviso de desalojo.

exemptions.description: Owner resides in the same rental unit with the tenant

clauses.note: A landlord who resides in the same rental unit with his or her tenant may evict said tenant without just cause

title: Unlawful Evictions, Notice, and Tenant Protections (San Francisco Rent Ordinance)
requirement: Landlords may not endeavor to recover possession or evict a tenant except on the specific enumerated just-cause grounds authorized under Section 37.9. Tenants must be provided required written notices, including a 10-day notice to cure for certain lease violations, and protected classes (such as qualifying elderly, disabled, or school-year educators/families) have specialized protections against certain no-fault evictions.
requirement_es: Es ilegal que un propietario intente desalojar o desaloje a un inquilino excepto bajo las causales justificadas explícitamente autorizadas bajo la Sección 37.9. Los inquilinos deben recibir las notificaciones requeridas por escrito, incluido un período de subsanación de 10 días para ciertas infracciones, y ciertas clases protegidas (adultos mayores, personas con discapacidades o familias/educadores durante el año escolar) tienen protecciones adicionales contra ciertos desalojos sin falta.
penalty: Misdemeanor subject to fines and penalties under Section 37.10A; civil action for injunctive relief, actual damages trebled (not less than three times actual damages), and reasonable attorney's fees and costs.
quoted_span:
It shall be unlawful for a landlord or any other person who willfully assists the landlord
to endeavor to recover possession or to evict a tenant except as provided in Section 37.9(a) and
(b).

title: Relocation Payments and Re-Rental Restrictions for Ellis Act Displacements
requirement: Landlords withdrawing units from the rental market under the Ellis Act must provide statutory relocation payments per eligible tenant (with extra payments for seniors or disabled tenants) and comply with strict re-rental and rent restrictions if the units are returned to the rental market within 5 to 10 years.
requirement_es: Los propietarios que retiran unidades del mercado de alquiler bajo la Ley Ellis deben proporcionar pagos legales de reubicación por inquilino elegible (con pagos adicionales para personas de la tercera edad o con discapacidades) y cumplir con estrictas restricciones de re-alquiler y límites de renta si las unidades vuelven a ofrecerse en alquiler dentro de 5 a 10 años.

key_value.label: Ellis Act relocation per tenant (effective Sept 1, 2022)

precedence.source_language: This Section 37.9A(a)(1) shall prevail over any conflicting provision of law authorizing the landlord to establish the rental rate upon the initial hiring of the unit.

penalty: Actual and exemplary damages in civil suits by displaced tenants or the City; punitive damages up to six months' contract rent for failure to notify Rent Board of intent to re-rent within 10 years.
quoted_span:
Where a landlord seeks eviction based upon

Section 37.9(a)(13), and the notice of intent to withdraw rental units is filed with the Rent Board

on or after September 1, 2022, the landlord shall pay relocation payments in the manner

described in Subsection 37.9A(e)(1)(A) and (B), except that the specific amount of the relocation

benefit shall be $10,000 per Eligible Tenant, and the total relocation payment shall be $30,000 in

the event there are more than three Eligible Tenants in the unit; and further, an Eligible Tenant

who meets any of the criteria listed in Subsection 37.9A(e)(1)(C) shall be entitled to receive an

additional payment of $6,700, in two payments of $3,350 each, the timing of which is set forth in

that subsection.

title: Relocation Expenses for Covered No-Fault Evictions
requirement: Eligible tenants who receive a covered no-fault eviction notice (such as owner/relative move-in, capital improvements, or substantial rehabilitation) are entitled to statutory relocation expenses, including an additional payment for senior, disabled, or household occupants with minor children.
requirement_es: Los inquilinos elegibles que reciban una notificación de desalojo sin falta cubierto (como mudanza del propietario o pariente, mejoras de capital o rehabilitación sustancial) tienen derecho a recibir gastos de reubicación reglamentarios, incluyendo pagos adicionales para personas mayores de 60 años, personas con discapacidades o menores en el hogar.

key_value.label: Base relocation payment per eligible tenant
key_value.value: $4,500 (max $13,500 per unit) plus $3,000 senior/disabled/child supplement (subject to annual CPI adjustment)

quoted_span:
Each Eligible Tenant who receives a Covered No-Fault Eviction Notice, in addition to

all rights under any other provision of law, shall be entitled to receive relocation expenses from

the landlord, in the amounts specified in section 37.9C(e).

title: Eviction Protections After Foreclosure
requirement: Tenants occupying a rental unit at the time of foreclosure cannot be evicted by the successor owner who took title through foreclosure without just cause under Section 37.9 or before the expiration of their existing lease, whichever is later, and must be provided written notice of their rights within 15 days.
requirement_es: Los inquilinos que ocupen una unidad al momento de una ejecución hipotecaria no pueden ser desalojados por el nuevo titular que obtuvo la propiedad tras la ejecución, salvo por causa justificada bajo la Sección 37.9 o al finalizar el contrato de arrendamiento existente (lo que ocurra más tarde), y deben recibir notificación por escrito de sus derechos dentro de 15 días.
penalty: Failure to provide mandatory foreclosure notices serves as a complete defense to an eviction under Section 37.9.
quoted_span:
Any residential tenant who was in possession of a rental unit at the time of

foreclosure may not be evicted by the person or entity who took title through foreclosure (see

Section 37.9D(a)), except for just cause as provided in Section 37.9 and related provisions of

Chapter 37, or at the end of the tenant's existing lease, whichever occurs later.

title: Prohibition of Fixed-Term Agreements Circumventing Just Cause
requirement: Lease provisions requiring a tenant to vacate at the end of a stated term or classifying failure to vacate at term expiration as just cause for eviction are void as contrary to public policy, unless Chapter 37 expressly authorizes a fixed term.
requirement_es: Las disposiciones contractuales que exigen que un inquilino desocupe la unidad al vencer un plazo fijo o que califiquen la falta de desocupación como justa causa de desalojo son nulas por ser contrarias al orden público, salvo que el Capítulo 37 autorice expresamente dicho plazo fijo.
penalty: Civil penalties up to two times amount paid or received; administrative penalties up to $100 per day (up to $1,000 per listing defect); reasonable attorney's fees.
quoted_span:
Consistent with Section 37.9(a)(2) and

Section 37.9(e), any provision of any lease or rental agreement that purports to require a tenant

to vacate a rental unit at the expiration of a stated term, or that purports to characterize a

tenant’s failure to vacate the rental unit at the end of the stated term as a just cause for eviction

(either of them, a “Fixed-Term Agreement”), shall be void as contrary to public policy, and a

landlord may not attempt to recover possession of the unit without just cause.
